title: Kernel handoff and decision tracing manual
author: Marco Chen
content:
Summary
-------
This document defines the kernel handoff model used by the Redwood serving runtime, the decision-tracing taxonomy we record for each request, and an operational playbook for diagnosing and repairing misrouted or stalled kernel executions. It combines architecture rationale, concrete observability requirements, and a step-by-step incident remediation procedure.

Scope
-----
Applies to: runtime kernel scheduler, request router, KV-cache manager, dispatcher, and observability collectors.
Excludes: higher-level API routing policies (handled in routing-policy-spec) and storage-layer persistence.

Goals
-----
- Ensure deterministic, searchable traces for every kernel decision that affects latency or fidelity.
- Provide clear remediation steps for common kernel-handoff faults (e.g., orphaned execution, priority inversion, kernel oscillation).
- Standardize the set of trace attributes collected across GPU types and sharded topologies so SRE and runtime teams can collaborate with minimal context switching.

Background and motivation
-------------------------
As the runtime supports heterogeneous GPU pools, model variants, and admission policies, requests frequently cross component boundaries: request classifier -> KV-cache -> scheduler -> kernel executor -> postprocessor. Historically, when a request hit a tail-latency anomaly, correlating which component made a specific decision (e.g., preempt, requeue, fallback to a lower-fidelity kernel) required ad-hoc logs. The decision-tracing model codifies the minimal set of attributes to record and provides a canonical span taxonomy so every execution path is queryable in our trace backend.

Decision-trace model (required attributes)
-----------------------------------------
Each decision event must be emitted as a trace span with the following attributes (key:value). All values are strings unless noted.
- trace_id: global 128-bit trace identifier (hex)
- request_id: request UUID
- span_id: span UUID
- parent_span_id: nullable span UUID
- timestamp_iso: ISO-8601 timestamp
- component: one of [classifier, kv-cache, scheduler, dispatcher, kernel, postprocessor, network-proxy]
- decision: canonical verb (e.g., admit, preempt, requeue, fallback_kernel, pin_shard, evict_kvcache)
- reason_code: short code (e.g., PCPU_HIGH, KV_MISS, MODEL_MISMATCH, PREEMPT_FOR_HIGHPRIO)
- kernel_hint: free-text kernel name / version / layout (optional)
- target_gpu: GPU identifier or pool tag (optional)
- estimated_latency_ms: integer (estimation produced at decision time)
- actual_latency_ms: integer (set on completion span only)
- owner_service: tenant or internal service that originated the request
- fidelity_level: one of [full, quantized-8, quantized-4, sparse]

Trace span taxonomy (recommended)
--------------------------------
- request.start (component=classifier): initial classification and admission decision
- cache.lookup (component=kv-cache): synchronous KV-cache check; emits evict_kvcache/kvcache_hit/kvcache_miss decisions
- schedule.plan (component=scheduler): computes slot, kernel_hint, and priority
- dispatch.attempt (component=dispatcher): attempts to bind to GPU slot; may emit requeue or fallback_kernel
- kernel.exec (component=kernel): start->complete lifecycle for a kernel run; must include estimated and actual latencies
- postprocess.apply (component=postprocessor): output transformations, safety filters, or sampling hooks
- request.finish (component=network-proxy): final response code and end-to-end latency

Handoff rules (canonical flow and invariants)
---------------------------------------------
1) Immutability at decision time: once a span with decision=admit or schedule.plan is emitted, the core decision fields (decision, reason_code, kernel_hint) must not be mutated; subsequent changes must be recorded as new spans (e.g., dispatch.attempt -> decision=requeue).
2) Single-writer for GPU binding: dispatcher must be the authoritative emitter of the bind event for a given kernel.exec span. Any other component writing bind/bound should include dispatch_span_id reference.
3) Latency estimations: scheduler must include estimated_latency_ms; executor records actual_latency_ms. Estimation delta (actual - estimated) propagates to an attached metric for calibration.
4) Fallback semantics: fallback_kernel spans must include fallback_chain attribute (comma-separated list of kernels attempted) and a fidelity_level tag for each fallback step.

Operational configurations (table)
---------------------------------
| config_key | default | description | owners | alert_threshold |
| khandoff.trace-sampling-pct | 5 | Percent of requests with full decision-traces emitted (for low-overhead prod) | runtime-observability | 95th latency >= 2x baseline |
| scheduler.max-requeues | 3 | Maximum scheduler requeues before forcing a fallback kernel | scheduler-team | >3 requeues per request |
| dispatcher.bind-timeout-ms | 1200 | Time to wait for GPU bind before requeueing | dispatcher-team | binds timed out >0.5% |
| kernel.exec-timeout-ms | 30000 | Wall-time cap for kernel execution before kill | runtime-safety | OOM or watchdog kills >0.1% |

Runbook: diagnosing misrouted kernels
-------------------------------------
This procedure is for incidents where requests are executed on an unexpected kernel (wrong fidelity or model variant) or stuck in dispatch/requeue loops.
1) Triage: obtain a sample trace_id from the failing request (from customer report or alert).
2) Trace inspection: query traces by trace_id. Look for schedule.plan span and the subsequent dispatch.attempt spans. Verify kernel_hint and fidelity_level recorded by schedule.plan match kernel.exec.
3) Check dispatcher logs: locate dispatch.bind events correlated by parent_span_id = schedule.plan.span_id. If bind failed, read reason_code (e.g., SLOT_EXHAUST, POOL_MISMATCH).
4) KV-cache correlation: if schedule.plan used cached prefix (kvcache_hit), confirm the cached fingerprint's kernel_hint matches current model variant. If mismatch, mark as KV_MISMATCH and file a corrective ticket (see "Corrective actions").
5) Requeue loop detection: count consecutive requeue decisions for request_id. If > scheduler.max-requeues, escalate to oncall and attach the trace + first and last dispatch.attempt spans.
6) Mitigation steps (fast):
   a) For SLOT_EXHAUST: temporarily expand pool tag (if autoscaling safe) or divert traffic to a fallback pool.
   b) For POOL_MISMATCH: trigger a small live reconfiguration to add the requested model variant to the target pool (requires change-request ticket for private deployments).
   c) For PREEMPT_FOR_HIGHPRIO: ensure high-priority tenant actually owns preempt budget; if misconfigured, rollback recent quota changes.

Corrective actions (post-incident)
---------------------------------
- File an operational postmortem with the trace_id, list of spans, and the root cause decision span.
- If KV_MISMATCH is root cause, run the cache audit job: 
  CLI: 
  rwd cache-audit --model model-name --since 24h --format json
  Expected output is a list of cached fingerprints with kernel_hint metadata. Reconcile mismatches by re-hashing prompt fingerprints or invalidating the affected keys.
- If dispatcher bug: attach dispatch logs and build id, and create a patch with a unit test that simulates the misrouting using the synthetic-dispatch test harness.

Trace retention and sampling guidance
-----------------------------------
- Full decision-traces (all spans listed above) are sampled at khandoff.trace-sampling-pct. All requests have a lightweight request.start and request.finish at 100% sampling (for billing/CSAT correlation).
- For on-demand debugging, the runtime supports a per-request debug-flag header: X-RWD-Debug: trace=full which forces full-span emission for that request (customer-facing header must be gated behind support tier).

Alerting matrix (examples)
-------------------------
- alert: dispatch.bind-timeout-rate-spike
  description: >
    Rate of dispatch.bind timeouts (bind-timeout-ms) exceeds 0.5% of requests over 5m.
  severity: P1
  runbook-ref: misrouted-kernels -> step 1-3

- alert: requeue-loop-detection
  description: >
    Fraction of requests with > scheduler.max-requeues in the last 10m.
  severity: P1
  runbook-ref: misrouted-kernels -> step 5

Examples and sample trace snippets
----------------------------------
Example schedule.plan span (JSON, illustrative):
{
  "trace_id": "a1b2c3d4e5f6...",
  "span_id": "span-0001",
  "component": "scheduler",
  "decision": "schedule.plan",
  "kernel_hint": "gptx-quant8-v2:layout=col32",
  "fidelity_level": "quantized-8",
  "estimated_latency_ms": "128",
  "reason_code": "KV_MISS"
}

Example dispatch.attempt sequence (pseudo):
- dispatch.attempt span_id=span-0002 parent=span-0001 decision=requeue reason_code=SLOT_EXHAUST
- dispatch.attempt span_id=span-0003 parent=span-0001 decision=requeue reason_code=SLOT_EXHAUST
- dispatch.attempt span_id=span-0004 parent=span-0001 decision=fallback_kernel reason_code=MAX_REQUEUES

Appendix: CLI and debug helpers
-------------------------------
- Query traces: rwd trace-get --id <trace_id> --backend jaeger | jq '.'
- Dump dispatch state for node: rwd node-dispatch-state --node-id <NODE> --since 5m
- Force a single-request full trace (dev only): 
  curl -H "X-RWD-Debug: trace=full" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
    https://runtime-internal.redwood/api/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"test"}'

Ownership and rollout plan
-------------------------
- Owners: scheduler-team (primary), dispatcher-team (secondary), runtime-observability (traces & alerts).
- Rollout: incremental — enable full-span emission for canary pool only (khandoff.trace-sampling-pct=50) for 1 week, then 10% across production for 48 hours, then the configured default.
- Migration notes: older kernels without span hooks must implement a shim that emits kernel.exec.start/kernel.exec.complete spans to satisfy the model.

----------------------------
